historian: Carchemish, 605 BC: the Babylonian Chronicle records Nebuchadnezzar’s rout of Egypt. Within weeks his father died and he took the throne. Critics once called Daniel's 'third year of Jehoiakim' a slip, since Jeremiah says the fourth. Babylonian accession-year counting, now well known from the chronicles, explains the difference.

Babylonian texts and 2 Kings agree: after an 18-month siege Jerusalem fell in 587 or 586 BC. The exact year is still debated. Ration tablets excavated in Babylon even name Jehoiachin, the exiled king of Judah, just as Second Kings records. And Nebuchadnezzar's own stamped bricks echo his boast in Daniel 4: great Babylon, that I have built.

The Nabonidus Chronicle says Babylon fell without a battle in October 539 BC. The Cyrus Cylinder is royal propaganda, but it confirms that deported peoples were sent home. For centuries Belshazzar was known only from Daniel, and nineteenth-century critics called him an invention. Then cylinders found at Ur in 1854 named him as Nabonidus's eldest son, left in charge of Babylon while his father was away. That is why the best Belshazzar could offer Daniel was to be the third ruler in the kingdom.

In 334 BC Alexander crossed the Hellespont. Persia had ruled from the Indus to Egypt for two centuries. Daniel 8 names this ram and goat outright: the kings of Media and Persia, and the king of Grecia.

At Issus in 333 BC Darius III fled the field. Arrian and Curtius describe it; the figures they give are inflated. Daniel had pictured a goat that broke the ram's two horns. Issus was the first great blow.
Tyre, Egypt, then Gaugamela in 331 BC. Babylon opened its gates; a Babylonian astronomical diary even notes the battle.

Alexander died in Babylon in 323 BC. Within a generation his empire had hardened into the Ptolemaic, Seleucid, Antigonid and other kingdoms. After the battle of Ipsus in 301 BC four main kingdoms stood, much as Daniel's four horns had said.

At Pydna in 168 BC the legion beat the phalanx. Polybius saw it as the moment Rome became master of the Mediterranean. Many critical scholars date the final form of Daniel to about 165 BC. Even on that view, Rome's long rule, its split and its fall all lay in the future. Copies of Daniel among the Dead Sea Scrolls date to the late second century BC.
Pompey entered the Temple in 63 BC, and Josephus records the shock. From then on Judea was a Roman client.
Actium and the fall of Alexandria in 30 BC ended the last Hellenistic kingdom. Egypt became Augustus’ personal province.

Josephus, an eyewitness, describes the burning of the Temple in AD 70. The Arch of Titus in Rome still shows the spoils. Daniel 9 had said that the people of a prince to come would destroy the city and the sanctuary.
After Theodosius died in AD 395 the empire was never again ruled as one. Historians debate how ‘final’ the split was.

In AD 476 Odoacer sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople. Contemporaries barely noticed; later writers made it the end of Rome. And true to the words 'they shall not cleave one to another', no power since, from Charlemagne to Napoleon, has welded the West into one lasting empire.
daniel: I was a youth when the king of Babylon came against Jerusalem, and I was carried away with the vessels of God's house. Yet I knew this: the God of heaven removes kings and sets up kings.

Word came to us by the river that the holy city was burned. I opened my window toward Jerusalem and prayed, for the Lord had not forgotten His people. One day the king's own bricks, stamped with his name, would bear witness to his boasting.

I stood in Belshazzar's hall and read the writing: numbered, weighed, divided. That night the gold fell, and the silver rose, as God had shown the king. In later ages wise men doubted that Belshazzar ever lived, until his father's cylinders spoke his name out of the dust of Ur.
Long after my days, I saw it in vision: a ram with two horns pushing west, north and south. Then a goat came from the west, not touching the ground.
The goat ran at the ram in the fury of his power and broke his two horns. No one could deliver the ram out of his hand.

I saw a leopard with four wings of a fowl, and dominion was given to it. Bronze now ruled over all the earth. The angel had named them to me plainly: the ram is Media and Persia, the rough goat is Grecia.
When the great horn was strong, it was broken. Four arose in its place, toward the four winds of heaven, but not with his power.

Then I saw a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, with great iron teeth. It devoured and broke in pieces, and it was diverse from all before it. My words were copied on scrolls hidden by the Dead Sea while Rome was still rising.
The iron set its foot on the glorious land. Still I was told: seal up the vision, for the time appointed is in God's hand.
The last kingdom of the goat passed into the hand of iron. Not one word of the dream had failed.
It was shown to me that Messiah would be cut off, and that the people of a prince to come would destroy the city and the sanctuary. So the house of God was burned once more.
The legs of iron stood apart, one in the east and one in the west. Strong still, yet already dividing.

Iron mixed with miry clay: they shall mingle, but not cleave together. And in the days of these kings, the God of heaven shall set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed. Every word has come to pass in its season. So the rest is sure.
nebuchadnezzar: At Carchemish I broke Pharaoh's army. From the Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt, the nations bowed to me. I am the head of gold. The scribes of Babylon wrote that day into their chronicle, and men read it still.

Jerusalem rebelled, so I burned its temple and carried its people to my city. Is not this great Babylon, that I have built by the might of my power? My name is stamped on every brick of my walls. Men dug them from the earth and read my boast, word for word.

I lived to see my pride broken; seven times passed over me in the field, until I knew the Most High rules. Now my heir is weighed and found wanting, and Persia takes my city in a single night. Scholars once said this Belshazzar never lived. The cylinders of Nabonidus, dug from the sand of Ur, proved them wrong.
From the dust I watch Persian kings sit in my palaces. Silver, lesser than gold, just as the Hebrew said.
A young king from the west comes against the silver. Even Persia, which humbled my house, trembles before him.
Bronze tramples silver at Gaugamela, and my Babylon opens its gates to a Greek. Kingdoms pass from hand to hand, and none of them is mine.
The conqueror of the world died in my palace in Babylon, not yet thirty-three. I too thought my kingdom eternal.
Iron rises in the west, stronger than any metal I knew. It breaks in pieces and subdues all things.
The iron enters Jerusalem, the city I once burned. Every empire of my dream has marched across that little land.
Egypt, the last of the Greek kingdoms, falls to Rome. The great image stands nearly whole, head to legs. Four kingdoms, in the order the Hebrew gave them. Not one out of place.
Rome burns the house of the Hebrew God, as I once did. But what hand can harm the God who humbled me?
Even iron splits in two, east and west. I dreamed of two legs.
Now come the feet, iron mixed with clay, kingdoms that will not hold. Then a stone cut without hands. I praise and extol the King of heaven, for all His works are truth.
kids: Long ago, a young prince named Nebuchadnezzar won a huge battle at a place called Carchemish. Soon he was king of Babylon, the golden head of the statue! And guess what? Clay tablets written by Babylonian scribes tell us about this battle.

Babylon's army surrounded Jerusalem and burned God's beautiful temple. Many people were taken far away to Babylon. Archaeologists even found clay tablets in Babylon listing food rations for Judah's captive king, Jehoiachin. The Bible got it right!

One night King Belshazzar threw a giant party. A hand appeared and wrote on the wall! That same night the Persians took the city. For a long time, some experts said Belshazzar was made up. Then they dug up a clay cylinder with his name on it!

Now a young king named Alexander marches out of Greece. Daniel saw him long before, as a goat running so fast its feet did not touch the ground. Daniel's book even names the kingdoms: Persia and Greece!
The goat charges the ram! At a place called Issus, Alexander beats the Persian king, Darius, who runs away. Just like Daniel's vision, nobody could rescue the ram.
Alexander wins again and again, all the way to Babylon. Now the bronze belly of the statue rules the world. Silver has given way to bronze, exactly in order.
Alexander dies young, in Babylon, when he is only thirty-two. His kingdom breaks into pieces, and four main kingdoms grow from it, like the four horns Daniel saw.
Here comes Rome, strong as iron! Roman soldiers beat the Greeks at a battle called Pydna. Iron is the strongest metal of all, and Rome was the strongest kingdom yet.
A Roman general named Pompey marches into Jerusalem. Now every kingdom in the statue has ruled over this small land, one after another.
Rome takes Egypt, the last Greek kingdom. Gold, silver, bronze and iron, in just the order Daniel said, hundreds of years before!

Rome's army burns Jerusalem and its temple. Daniel had said the city and the sanctuary would be destroyed. In Rome you can still see a stone arch that shows soldiers carrying away treasures from the temple.
The Roman Empire splits into two parts, east and west, like the statue's two iron legs.

Finally the western empire breaks into many kingdoms, like the feet of iron mixed with clay. Iron and clay don't stick together, and those kingdoms never joined into one again. Next comes the best part: God's kingdom, the stone that fills the whole earth!

furnace.title: The Fiery Furnace
furnace.historian: After the dream, Nebuchadnezzar set up an image of gold on the plain of Dura, as if to say his kingdom would never pass. Three young Hebrews would not bow, and were thrown into a furnace. Burning as a royal punishment is attested: Jeremiah 29:22 says this same king roasted two rebels in the fire.
furnace.daniel: My friends Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah would not bow to the image of gold. The king heated the furnace seven times hotter, yet when he looked, he saw four men walking in the fire, and the form of the fourth was like the Son of God.
furnace.nebuchadnezzar: I made the whole image of gold, not only the head. Let all bow! Three Hebrews refused, and I cast them into the fire. Then I saw four men walking loose in the flames. I came near and called them out: there is no other God that can deliver after this sort.
furnace.kids: King Nebuchadnezzar built a huge golden statue and told everyone to bow down. Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego said no, they would only worship God. So into the hot furnace they went! But the king saw four people walking in the fire, safe and free. God was with them!

tree.title: The Great Tree
tree.historian: Daniel 4 tells of a dream of a great tree cut down, and a king humbled for seven times. No Babylonian record of Nebuchadnezzar's illness has been confirmed. But among the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Prayer of Nabonidus tells a similar story about a later Babylonian king struck for seven years at Teima.
tree.daniel: The king dreamed of a tree that reached to heaven, and a watcher cried: hew it down, but leave the stump. I told him: the tree is thou, O king. Break off thy sins by righteousness. A year later he walked on his palace roof and boasted, and the word was fulfilled.
tree.nebuchadnezzar: I walked on my palace and said: is not this great Babylon, that I have built? While the word was in my mouth, my kingdom departed. I ate grass like an ox, until I lifted my eyes to heaven and my reason returned. Now I praise the King of heaven.
tree.kids: Nebuchadnezzar dreamed about a giant tree that was chopped down. Daniel explained: the tree is you, King! The king got very proud, and for seven years he lived outside like an animal. When he looked up to God, he got better, and he praised God.

wall.title: The Writing on the Wall
wall.historian: Herodotus and Xenophon both describe Babylon feasting on the night it fell to Cyrus in 539 BC. Belshazzar himself, once dismissed as fiction, is named on the Nabonidus Cylinder from Ur. Mene, tekel, peres are Aramaic weights: numbered, weighed, divided.
wall.daniel: The king drank from the vessels of the Lord's house, and fingers of a man's hand wrote upon the plaster of the wall. Mene, God hath numbered thy kingdom. Tekel, thou art weighed in the balances. Peres, thy kingdom is given to the Medes and Persians. That night Belshazzar was slain.
wall.nebuchadnezzar: My heir feasted with the gold cups I took from Jerusalem. He knew what happened to me, yet he did not humble his heart. The hand wrote, and the silver kingdom walked in through my gates that same night.
wall.kids: King Belshazzar had a huge party and used the golden cups from God's temple. Suddenly a hand appeared and wrote on the wall! Only Daniel could read it: your kingdom is finished. That very night the Persians came in, and the kingdom of silver began.

den.title: The Lions' Den
den.historian: Under the new Persian order, a decree of the Medes and Persians could not be altered. Who 'Darius the Mede' was is still debated: no inscription names him, and scholars suggest Cyrus's governor Gubaru or Cyrus himself. Kings of the region did keep lions; Assyrian palace reliefs show lions released from cages for the royal hunt.
den.daniel: Jealous men made the king sign a law that no one could pray to any god but him. I knelt at my open window three times a day, as I always had. They cast me to the lions, but my God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths.
den.nebuchadnezzar: Now Persia rules my city, and Daniel, whom I set over the wise men, still serves. A Persian king cast him to the lions and could not sleep all night. In the morning he cried: is thy God able? And Daniel answered from the den.
den.kids: Daniel kept praying to God, even when a new law said he must not. So he was thrown into a den full of hungry lions! The king worried all night. In the morning Daniel was fine: God sent an angel to close the lions' mouths!

events.text: Thou, O king, art a king of kings: for the God of heaven hath given thee a kingdom, power, and strength, and glory. And wheresoever the children of men dwell, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the heaven hath he given into thine hand, and hath made thee ruler over them all. Thou art this head of gold.

In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon unto Jerusalem, and besieged it. And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with part of the vessels of the house of God: which he carried into the land of Shinar to the house of his god; and he brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.

And this is the writing that was written, MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE; God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it. TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting. PERES; Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians. In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain. And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old.
And as I was considering, behold, an he goat came from the west on the face of the whole earth, and touched not the ground: and the goat had a notable horn between his eyes.

And he came to the ram that had two horns, which I had seen standing before the river, and ran unto him in the fury of his power. And I saw him come close unto the ram, and he was moved with choler against him, and smote the ram, and brake his two horns: and there was no power in the ram to stand before him, but he cast him down to the ground, and stamped upon him: and there was none that could deliver the ram out of his hand.

The ram which thou sawest having two horns are the kings of Media and Persia. And the rough goat is the king of Grecia: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king. And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee, and another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth.

Therefore the he goat waxed very great: and when he was strong, the great horn was broken; and for it came up four notable ones toward the four winds of heaven. Now that being broken, whereas four stood up for it, four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not in his power.
And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron: forasmuch as iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things: and as iron that breaketh all these, shall it break in pieces and bruise.

After this I saw in the night visions, and behold a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth: it devoured and brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with the feet of it: and it was diverse from all the beasts that were before it; and it had ten horns.
Thus he said, The fourth beast shall be the fourth kingdom upon earth, which shall be diverse from all kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth, and shall tread it down, and break it in pieces.

And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.

His legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay. And whereas thou sawest the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided; but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron, forasmuch as thou sawest the iron mixed with miry clay.

And as the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay, so the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken. And whereas thou sawest iron mixed with miry clay, they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay. And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.

assembled.text: Thou, O king, sawest, and behold a great image. This great image, whose brightness was excellent, stood before thee; and the form thereof was terrible. This image’s head was of fine gold, his breast and his arms of silver, his belly and his thighs of brass, His legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay.

exploded.text: This is the dream; and we will tell the interpretation thereof before the king. Thou, O king, art a king of kings: for the God of heaven hath given thee a kingdom, power, and strength, and glory. And wheresoever the children of men dwell, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the heaven hath he given into thine hand, and hath made thee ruler over them all. Thou art this head of gold. And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee, and another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth. And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron: forasmuch as iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things: and as iron that breaketh all these, shall it break in pieces and bruise.

stone.text: Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces. Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken to pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors; and the wind carried them away, that no place was found for them: and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth. And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.

And wheresoever the children of men dwell, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the heaven hath he given into thine hand, and hath made thee ruler over them all. Thou art this head of gold.

chest.text: And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee, and another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth. The ram which thou sawest having two horns are the kings of Media and Persia.

belly.text: And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee, and another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth. And the rough goat is the king of Grecia: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king.

furnace.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonied, and rose up in haste, and spake, and said unto his counsellors, Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire? They answered and said unto the king, True, O king. He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God.

tree.text: Thus were the visions of mine head in my bed; I saw, and behold a tree in the midst of the earth, and the height thereof was great. The tree grew, and was strong, and the height thereof reached unto heaven, and the sight thereof to the end of all the earth: The leaves thereof were fair, and the fruit thereof much, and in it was meat for all: the beasts of the field had shadow under it, and the fowls of the heaven dwelt in the boughs thereof, and all flesh was fed of it. And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up mine eyes unto heaven, and mine understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the most High, and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation:

wall.text: In the same hour came forth fingers of a man’s hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king’s palace: and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote. And this is the writing that was written, MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE; God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it. TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting. PERES; Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.

den.text: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.
